claim: A stable latent motion model plus learned SPD stiffness encoder can reproduce and modulate demonstrated variable-impedance skills for via-points and obstacle avoidance, with simulation and preliminary Franka co-manipulation evidence; absolute variable-impedance stability and statistically reliable HRI benefit remain unestablished.
epistemic_status: Primary simulation, synthetic stiffness, and preliminary human–robot hardware evidence with inferred stiffness labels and limited reporting.
problem_and_setting: Learning both motion and compliant interaction from demonstrations while adapting trajectories to via-points, new starts/goals, and static obstacles without retraining.
method_or_mechanism: An invertible neural-network dynamical system maps motion to a latent straight-line stable flow and modulates it through via/tangent points. A stiffness encoder maps position, velocity, and force to Cholesky factors enforcing SPD stiffness; a decoder implements the interaction model and outputs control force/torque. Ground-truth stiffness is absent and targets are inferred from estimated references and a model.
content_summary: LASA handwriting simulations test reproduction and modulation. A self-made 2-DoF mass-spring-damper dataset reports about 90% stiffness-estimation accuracy versus traditional methods, without metric/sample details in the packet. Human–Franka transport covers regular and changed human style, changed start/goal, obstacle avoidance, and zero-gravity comparison. Integrated interaction-energy values are 0.395, 0.214, and 0.151 N·s; authors call the obstacle-aware condition most relaxed, but the packet does not unambiguously map every value. Absolute stability is not studied, hyperparameters are trial-and-error, and training is slow.
synthesis_role: Evidence for jointly learning stable motion geometry and SPD impedance mappings, and for the unresolved gap between stable motion generation and closed-loop variable-impedance stability.
development_link: Combines invertible stable dynamical systems, constraint-preserving stiffness output, and geometry-based modulation without retraining.

evidence.finding: Latent stable flow supports via-point and circular-obstacle modulation; Cholesky output enforces SPD stiffness.
Demonstrated motions are reproduced and modulated through via-points and around obstacles.
Approximately 90% stiffness-estimation accuracy is reported versus traditional methods, with metric/sample details absent from the packet.
Transport is demonstrated under changed human style, start/goal, and obstacle conditions; integrated interaction energies 0.395, 0.214, and 0.151 N·s are reported.
Absolute variable-impedance stability is not studied; hyperparameters are trial-and-error and training is comparatively slow.

boundary_conditions: One Franka transport setup with unreported participant count.
assumptions: Estimated reference motion/model yields meaningful stiffness labels.
Latent motion stability transfers adequately through inverse mapping.
SPD stiffness is sufficient for desired interaction behavior.
Integrated interaction energy is a useful workload proxy.

reported: Absolute variable-impedance stability is not studied.
Hyperparameters are chosen by trial and error.
Training is slower than state of art.
inferred: Stiffness accuracy depends on inferred-label assumptions.
Human evidence is preliminary without participant/repetition/statistical details.
Energy comparison cannot establish population-level superiority.
Stable motion generation does not itself certify closed-loop interaction stability.

verification_status: Controller-verified identity and full-text hash; packet ambiguity in energy-value mapping is preserved.
